plain_meaning: I went to him fully planning to stay cold and sulk, but my heart forgot all that and ran straight to making up.
speaker_context: A woman telling her close friend about a lovers' quarrel.
real_life_example: You swore you'd give them the silent treatment after the fight, but the second they text 'hey', you reply in two seconds.

plain_meaning: When I sit alone and think about him, my own heart feels like it is eating me up.
speaker_context: A woman alone with her thoughts, talking about her own heart.
real_life_example: Lying awake at 2 a.m. replaying the argument while longing and regret keep gnawing at you.

plain_meaning: My eyes picked him and brought on this ocean of love-pain, and now those same eyes can't sleep and keep suffering.
speaker_context: A woman blaming her own eyes for her heartache.
real_life_example: You were the one who wanted to meet them, and now you can't sleep and keep checking their last seen.

plain_meaning: Even when someone just lets the quarrel dry up and never makes the first move, my heart still wants to be back together with them.
speaker_context: A woman after a quarrel who still longs to reconcile.
real_life_example: They've left you on read for days after the fight, and you still want to patch things up.

plain_meaning: What is the use of having him, or finally being together, if my heart has already broken into pieces?
speaker_context: A woman whose long waiting has worn her down.
real_life_example: After weeks of waiting for someone to show up, even their arrival can't undo how tired and hurt you feel.

plain_meaning: I even forgot my sense of shame, because my foolish heart just can't learn to forget him.
speaker_context: A woman admitting she can't control her heart.
real_life_example: You swore you'd never text first, and then you do it anyway at midnight.

plain_meaning: If you pretend to know things you never learned, people start doubting even the things you really do know well.
speaker_context: General advice, not a story.
real_life_example: You bluff about a skill in an interview; once they catch it, they stop trusting your real strengths too.

plain_meaning: Friends who are warm only when they need something, and vanish when you need them, aren't worth much, and it hardly matters whether you keep or lose them.
speaker_context: General advice about fair-weather friends.
real_life_example: The friend who texts only when they want your notes or a favour, and goes quiet when you're struggling.

plain_meaning: Good fortune finds its way to wise people who know what is right and never crave what belongs to others.
speaker_context: General advice about honesty and greed.
real_life_example: The colleague who never takes shortcuts or credit for others' work, and slowly earns everyone's trust and the promotion.

plain_meaning: Real friendship is like your hand grabbing your clothes the instant they slip: it rushes to fix your trouble without being asked.
speaker_context: General statement about true friends.
real_life_example: You forget your ID before an exam, and your friend is already running to sort it out before you even say anything.

plain_meaning: The world praises people whose kindness comes with good deeds that actually help others.
speaker_context: General statement about good character.
real_life_example: Someone who helps you with a problem without making you feel small or in debt.

plain_meaning: The world keeps going because of people with good character; without them it would crumble into the soil.
speaker_context: General statement about good character.
real_life_example: The classmate or neighbour whose honesty and kindness holds a whole group together.

plain_meaning: Even toward people who are unfriendly and unfair to you, failing to behave with grace is the lowest thing you can do.
speaker_context: General advice about staying decent.
real_life_example: Someone ghosts you or talks behind your back, and you still stay civil instead of stooping to their level.

plain_meaning: Last night, aching with desire, I sighed and suffered like a trapped doe. Mother seemed to sense my pain and asked, 'Aren't you sleeping, my girl?' I couldn't say the truth out loud, so I told myself: how can eyes sleep for someone who keeps thinking of the lord of the forest hills?
speaker_context: A young woman telling her closest friend about a sleepless night of longing.
real_life_example: A parent knocks at midnight asking why you're still awake, and you say 'just can't sleep' when you're really thinking about one person.

plain_meaning: Suffer now, my heart: you were the one that melted at the smile of that young girl with deer-like eyes, graceful shoulders and soft, few words, as lovely as the rich town of Arcot.
speaker_context: A man scolding his own heart for falling for her.
real_life_example: You crushed on someone hard, and now you're the one stuck overthinking while they don't notice.
meaning_source: , unverified (moderate confidence on the words, low on the exact situation)

plain_meaning: Now that we've finished what we set out to do, may the house-lizard on the tall wall give its good-omen chirp, so the worry of the one waiting at home can end. In the evening the whole village smells of jasmine garlands.
speaker_context: A husband returning home, hoping his wife's anxious waiting is about to end.
real_life_example: You're on the last train home after a long time away, hoping the person waiting knows you're nearly there.

plain_meaning: Friend, he's finally back! He crossed those huge, dangerous hills just to come to us, after we ached for him every time we looked at our loose gold bangle and heard our little son's sweet voice.
speaker_context: A wife telling her friend that her husband has returned from a long journey.
real_life_example: Someone who spent months abroad for work finally lands, and the family who've been counting days rushes to the door.

plain_meaning: The speaker wishes she could stop pining for her uncaring lover from the seashore and be free of the pain of loving him.
speaker_context: A woman talking to her friend about a lover who doesn't care.
real_life_example: You wish you could just stop thinking about someone who clearly isn't putting in the effort.
meaning_source: , unverified (low confidence, please have this one checked)

plain_meaning: We trusted the words of the mountain lord and lost our glow. Now the village women gossip all night and spread nasty rumours; let the scandal grow, what has this noisy village lost anyway?
speaker_context: A young woman bitterly answering the gossip about her secret relationship.
real_life_example: Rumours about you and someone spread through the group chat, and you shrug: 'let them talk, what have they lost?'

plain_meaning: Owl on the old sacred tree by our village waterfront: please don't hoot your scary call tonight. We'll feed you rich offerings, because I'm awake and anxious, waiting for my lover to arrive.
speaker_context: A young woman talking to an owl while she waits for her lover at night.
real_life_example: You're waiting for someone to arrive late at night and every sound outside makes your heart jump.

plain_meaning: If only I could find someone to go to that slender girl with eyes like blue lilies and tell her 'he has come': she wouldn't ask 'who is this?', she'd be completely overwhelmed with joy.
speaker_context: A man wishing for a messenger to tell his beloved he has arrived.
real_life_example: You wish a friend would just tell them 'they're here', because you can't bring yourself to message first.

plain_meaning: He keeps his word and grows dearer as time passes; he has never been apart from me. Good people's friendship is like honey set in sandal, and as the world needs water, he needs me. Afraid my forehead would turn pale with sorrow, he never does anything to hurt me.
speaker_context: A woman praising her lover to her friend.
real_life_example: Your partner who texts 'reached home' every time and shows up when they say they will.

plain_meaning: In the lonely dry land where village kids play, as evening came on I thought of her, the sweet one at home, just as she lights the lamp at dusk, as if my work were already done.
speaker_context: A man travelling for work, remembering his wife at dusk.
real_life_example: Working abroad, you picture your family sitting down for dinner at exactly the time evening falls back home.
